docs.title: Count people, not motion.
docs.text:
Apex Crosswalk counts people as they enter and leave, so your lights, heating, and fans respond to real occupancy. Private, local, and energy efficient.

  • Crosswalk Gateway

  • Crosswalk Sensor

  • Apex CoreComing Soon

Privacy Focused. Energy Savings. No Subscriptions.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and Help
docs.text: If you're having issues with your Apex hardware, we're here to help. Because our devices are designed for local-first, privacy-focused home automation, most issues can be resolved with a few simple steps.

docs.title: Common Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Before reaching out, please check the following:

  • Connectivity: Ensure your Gateway is powered on, connected to your home Wi-Fi, and within range of your sensors.
  • Power: For battery-powered sensors, plug the sensor into USB and check that it charges — 🟡 Yellow means charging, 🟢 Green means full. For hardwired sensors, check that the 🔴 Red and 🟢 Green lights are on; if they're off, check the USB-C cable and power adapter.
  • Firmware: Ensure your device is running the latest firmware. The Gateway can update itself from its dashboard.

docs.title: Quick Fixes
docs.text:
• Gateway Issues: For Wi-Fi, dashboard, or MQTT problems, see the Crosswalk Gateway Troubleshooting Guide.
  • Sensor Issues: For count inaccuracies, pairing failures, or orientation help, refer to the Crosswalk Sensor Troubleshooting Guide.
  • Checking Sensor Status: Crosswalk sensor lights only show power, not pairing or counting, so the sensor light reference explains what you can and cannot tell from the hardware itself.

Common Suggestions

  • Reboot: Sometimes a simple power cycle (unplug and replug) is all that's needed to bring the Gateway back onto the network.
  • Proximity: When pairing new sensors, keep them in the same room as the Gateway for the most reliable initial handshake.
  • Dashboard First: The apex.local dashboard is the fastest way to see what every sensor and room is currently reporting.

A Note on Privacy

Apex Sensor Labs hardware does not have a cloud portal. This means we cannot "remotely access" your device to troubleshoot it. All support happens through local debugging on your own network, with us walking you through it.

docs.title: Reporting Issues
docs.text:
During the Crosswalk beta, email is the fastest way to reach us. Please include:

  • Which device you're having trouble with (Gateway or Sensor)
  • The firmware version shown on your apex.local dashboard

  • What you expected to happen, and what happened instead

  • Email: support@apexsensorlabs.com

  • Website: apexsensorlabs.com

DIY Community

A community space for Apex users to share automations and setups is on the way. Until then, email us — beta feedback goes straight to the engineer building the hardware.

docs.title: Count people, not motion.
docs.text:
Apex Crosswalk counts people as they enter and leave, so your lights, heating, and fans respond to real occupancy. Private, local, and energy efficient.

By counting people as they pass through a doorway, it eliminates the "ghosting" and delays associated with traditional motion sensors.

docs.title: Unboxing
docs.text:
The Crosswalk Sensor is a high-precision occupancy detector. It comes in two versions:

  • Battery-Powered: Runs for months on a rechargeable battery, with no wires to the doorway.
  • Hardwired: Stays plugged into USB-C power, so there is no battery to charge.

Battery-PoweredHardwired
  • 1x Crosswalk Sensor Board: Featuring dual sensing zones.
  • 1x 3D Printed Case & Lid: For sleek mounting.
  • 1x LiPo Battery: Provides months of wireless operation.
  • 2x Adhesive Mounting Strips
  • USB-C Charging Cable NOT included
  • 1x Crosswalk Sensor Board: Featuring dual sensing zones.
  • 1x 3D Printed Case & Lid: For sleek mounting.
  • 2x Adhesive Mounting Strips
  • USB-C Cable and USB Power Adapter NOT included

docs.title: Setup Process
docs.text:
Follow the linear walkthrough to get your Crosswalk sensor up and running.

Set up your Gateway first

Your sensors talk to the Crosswalk Gateway, not directly to your Wi-Fi. The Gateway needs to be online before a sensor can pair or report counts.

  • Start Step 1: Flashing

docs.title: Step 1: Flashing Your Gateway
docs.text:
The Crosswalk Gateway is the "hub" for your Apex Crosswalk sensors. First, you need to connect the antenna. You may need to remove the case lid in order to best secure the antenna.

Once the antenna is connected, remove the lid so you can access to device's BOOT button, circled below. If you have a paperclip or other device, you can access the BOOT button that way through the lid as well.

Why we Flash First

To ensure you have the absolute latest features and the most secure, privacy-focused version of our local software, we start every setup by quickly updating the device's firmware. This ensures your hardware is running the best possible version of the Crosswalk Gateway before it joins your home.

Browser Requirement

You must use Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a computer to flash your device. We do not support other browsers for flashing.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
• Crosswalk Gateway Hub
  • USB-C Cable
  • Computer with Chrome or Edge installed.

docs.title: Flashing Procedure
docs.text:
1. Connect: Hold the BOOT button of your device, circled in red above. With the button held down, plug the Gateway into your computer's USB port. Let go of the boot button once it's plugged in.

  2. Start Flash: Click the Install button below.

    Install Crosswalk Gateway

  3. Select Device: A small window will pop up. Select the entry that says "USB Serial" or "Enhanced COM Port" and click Connect.

  4. Install Gateway Firmware: Click Install Crosswalk Gateway

  5. Click Confirm: Click Confirm to finish installation.

  6. Wait: Do not unplug the device until the screen says "Installation Complete".

  7. Finish: Your Gateway is now ready to connect to your home network.

  • Next Step: Connecting & Setup (Step 2)

docs.title: Step 2: Connecting and Setup
docs.text: Now you need to connect your Gateway to your home Wi-Fi and set up its connection to your smart home app.

docs.title: 1. Wi-Fi Configuration
docs.text:
1. Power On: Plug your Gateway into any USB power outlet. You will need to unplug your device and plug it back in after installing the firmware.

  2. Find the Hotspot: On your phone or computer, open your Wi-Fi settings. Look for a network starting with Apex-Setup — each Gateway adds its own four-character suffix, so yours will look something like Apex-Setup-ca3f.

  3. Connect: Join that network. Once connected, open a web browser on your phone and visit "http://192.168.4.1".

  4. Enter Credentials: Pick your home's 2.4GHz Wi-Fi network from the list, type your password, and click Connect.

    List says 'No networks found'?

    Give the Gateway a few seconds to finish scanning and reload the page. You can also type your network name into the top box by hand.

  5. Reboot: The Gateway will save the settings and restart. It is now connected to your home network. Reconnect to your home Wi-Fi network on your phone.

docs.title: 2. The Apex Dashboard
docs.text:
Your Gateway has its own "Control Panel" that you can access from any browser in your house.

  1. Open Browser: Type http://apex.local into your browser's address bar.

    Trouble finding the dashboard?

    If http://apex.local doesn't load, your router may not support local names. You can find the IP address of your Gateway in your router's device list (it will appear as 'Crosswalk-Gateway') and type that number into your browser instead.

  2. The Main Screen: You should now see the Apex Gateway dashboard, with the Rooms, Sensors, Settings, and Status tabs across the top.

docs.title: 3. Smart Home Connection (MQTT)
docs.text:
To send the person counts to Home Assistant or other apps, you need to set up "MQTT".

  1. Go to Settings: On the dashboard, click Settings and then MQTT.

  2. Type Broker Info: Enter your MQTT Broker's address (usually the IP of your Home Assistant server).

  3. Save: Click Save. The dashboard should now say "MQTT Connected".

docs.title: 4. Gateway Connected
docs.text:
Your Apex Crosswalk Gateway is now connected and set up. It uses the Home Assistant discovery message by default, so your Gateway and your Crosswalk sensors appear automatically in Home Assistant or any smart home hub of your choice. Go check it out in your smart home!

Your Apex Gateway lists information for you here to include 'Total Occupancy'. This is an aggregation of all room counts between all of your Crosswalk Sensors. If two people are in your 'Office' and one person is in the 'Living Room' this count would be 3. This also lists and links to all of your Crosswalk sensor devices. You can easily click 'Reset All Rooms' to revert the room counts to 0 across your entire setup.

docs.title: 5. Add Rooms
docs.text:
Now we need to add and configure rooms before adding a sensor. Go to the Rooms tab at the top and add some rooms!

  1. Add a Room: Type in the room name and click 'Add'

  1. Configure Rooms: Now that you have rooms set up, you can reset the counts, increment, decrement the room count, rename the room, or delete the room. This all syncs over MQTT to your smart home setup.

  1. Set up Sensors: Now it's time to go set up your Crosswalk sensors. Click the link below to start setting up a sensor.
  • Next Step: Set up your Sensors
  • Keeping the Gateway Updated

docs.title: Crosswalk Gateway Troubleshooting
docs.text: If your Gateway is having trouble connecting to Wi-Fi or coordinating sensors, follow these steps.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
1. Immediately after flashing, it should host its own Wi-Fi connection. Make sure you switch to this using your phone.
  2. Once connected, visit http://192.168.4.1 in your phone's web browser. This will allow you to set up the Wi-Fi for the gateway.
  3. Once this is done, remember to re-connect to your home's Wi-Fi on your phone.

docs.title: I Can't Open apex.local
docs.text:
1. Check Connection: Make sure your computer or phone is on the same Wi-Fi network as the Gateway.
  2. Use the IP Address: If http://apex.local fails, look at your router's device list for "Crosswalk-Gateway" and type its IP address (e.g., http://192.168.1.50) into your browser.

docs.title: MQTT Connection Problems
docs.text: If your dashboard says "MQTT Disconnected": 1. Verify Broker IP: Ensure the IP address of your Home Assistant (or broker) hasn't changed. 2. Check Credentials: Double-check your Username and Password in the Gateway settings menu. 3. Port 1883: Ensure your broker is listening on the standard port (1883) and is not blocked by a firewall. 4. The gateway has the ability to 'Test Connection' for MQTT. Enter your MQTT settings and click Test Connection prior to saving. Saving will reboot your device.

docs.title: Firmware Updates
docs.text:
The Gateway updates itself from its own dashboard — see Updating Firmware. If an update is interrupted and the Gateway no longer comes back online, you can always recover it by reflashing over USB from the Flashing page.

Restart

Most Gateway issues can be fixed by simply unplugging it for 10 seconds and plugging it back in to refresh the network connection.

docs.title: Updating Firmware
docs.text:
Your Crosswalk Gateway updates itself over your home network. You do not need to plug it back into a computer or use the install button again.

Current Version

The latest Gateway firmware is 1.2.10. Your Gateway shows the version it is currently running on the dashboard.

docs.title: 1. Open the Dashboard
docs.text:
Type http://apex.local into any browser on your home network.

Trouble finding the dashboard?

If http://apex.local doesn't load, look for Crosswalk-Gateway in your router's device list and type its IP address into your browser instead.

docs.title: 2. Check for an Update
docs.text: Go to Settings and open the firmware update section. The Gateway checks with Apex Sensor Labs and tells you whether a newer version is available.

docs.title: 3. Install
docs.text:
Start the update and leave the Gateway alone. It downloads the new firmware, installs it, and restarts on its own.

Keep it powered

Do not unplug the Gateway while it is updating. Interrupting an update partway through can leave the device needing a USB reflash to recover.

docs.title: 4. Confirm
docs.text:
Once the Gateway restarts, reload http://apex.local and check that the version number on the dashboard has changed.

If the dashboard doesn't come back after a couple of minutes, unplug the Gateway for 10 seconds and plug it back in.

docs.title: What About the Sensors?
docs.text:
Crosswalk sensors do not update over the air. To update a sensor, connect it to your computer over USB and use the install button on the Sensor Flashing page, exactly as you did during first-time setup.

  • Gateway Troubleshooting
  • Back to Home Page

docs.title: Getting Started with Crosswalk Gateway
docs.text: The Crosswalk Gateway is the heart of your person-counting ecosystem. It acts as the bridge between your battery-powered Crosswalk sensors (using ESP-NOW) and your smart home controller (over MQTT).

docs.title: Unboxing
docs.text:
The Crosswalk Gateway is the central coordinator for your person-counting sensors.

  • 1x Crosswalk Gateway: Powered by an ESP32-S3.
  • 1x Crosswalk Gateway Case: Fits the Crosswalk Gateway board
  • 1x u.FL/IPEX to SMA adapter: Attaches ESP32-S3 to Antenna
  • 1x 2.4GHz Antenna: For Wi-Fi and ESP-NOW
  • USB-C Cable NOT included: You'll need one to flash the Gateway and to power it afterwards.

docs.title: Setup Process
docs.text:
To get started, follow our linear walkthrough to flash and configure your Gateway.

  1. Flashing: Install the latest firmware.
  2. Connecting & Setup: Connect to Wi-Fi and MQTT.

Dependency

You must complete this Gateway setup before attempting to install your Crosswalk Sensors. Sensors will not be able to transmit data until a Gateway is online and within range.

  • Start Step 1: Flashing

docs.title: Step 3: Assembly
docs.text: Now that your sensor is paired with the Gateway, it's time to assemble the hardware and close up the case.

docs.title: Parts Needed
docs.text:
• Flashed and paired Crosswalk Board
  • LiPo Battery (Battery-Powered version only)
  • 3D Printed Case & Lid

Pair before you assemble

If you haven't paired the sensor to your Gateway yet, do that first in Step 2 — the power connection is much easier to reach before the case is closed.

docs.title: Assembly Procedure
docs.text:
Make sure there is no film on top of either VL53L1X sensor. This comes on during shipping and will impede the sensor's ability to correctly take measurements. Remove this film very carefully, and try to not touch the sensor itself with your finger.

  1. Board Placement: The Crosswalk sensor is built from the "bottom" up. Place the board upside-down on the posts.

  2. Battery Lid: Place the battery lid on top of the board. It should fit in the posts and align on top of the board. The Hardwired version uses the battery lid too, even though it has no battery.

  3. Place Battery (Battery-Powered only): Place the battery on top of the lid and plug in the JST connector. If you have the Hardwired version, skip this step.

  4. Slide on the Lid: Slide the "top" lid in. Please note for the first time sliding in it may not slide in easily.

  5. Mounting Strip: Place one of the two mounting strips on the back-side of the case. This will make it easy to remove from the doorway for charging or servicing.

  • Next Step: Mounting (Step 4)

docs.title: Step 2: Pairing & Configuration
docs.text: Before you assemble and mount the sensor, you need to link it to your Gateway. It's much easier to pair your Crosswalk sensor while the board is still open and you can reach its power connection.

docs.title: 1. Linking to the Gateway
docs.text:
To add a new sensor, you must first put the Gateway into "Pairing Mode."

  1. Open Dashboard: Navigate to http://apex.local on your browser. Go to the Sensors tab.

  1. Open the Pairing Window: In the Add Sensor card, click Open Pairing Window (60s).

  1. The Countdown: A 60-second countdown will appear on your screen that allows a Crosswalk Sensor to start pairing.

  2. Activate the Sensor: While the timer is counting down, power on your Crosswalk sensor. It will automatically boot up and initiate the pairing sequence with the Crosswalk Gateway.

    Battery-PoweredHardwired

    Plug the battery into the JST connector.

    Watch the dashboard, not the sensor

    Once it's running on battery, the sensor keeps all of its lights off to save power — so there is no light to tell you it is awake and working. The Gateway dashboard is where you confirm pairing.

    Plug a USB-C cable into the sensor and into a USB power adapter.

    Watch the dashboard, not the sensor

    The red power light and the green light come on as soon as the sensor has power. They only mean the board is powered, not that it has paired. The Gateway dashboard is where you confirm pairing.

    • Note: The sensor will scan for the Gateway automatically.

  3. Success: When successful, the dashboard will display "Sensor Paired Successfully" and the new device will appear in your list.

  1. Home Assistant: Check out your new sensor in Home Assistant!

The Apex Crosswalk Gateway should now show a connected sensor as well.

Check out a Room.

Now go look at the sensor.

docs.title: 2. Device Settings
docs.text:
Now you can customize how this sensor behaves in your home. Go back to the Apex Gateway web page.

  1. Identify & Name: Click on the new sensor in the list. Give it a clear name like "Office Door" or "Office - Bathroom Door".

docs.title: 3. Counting Modes
docs.text:
Crosswalk sensors can operate in different modes depending on your doorway layout. You can set the mode now, but it's easiest to confirm it is correct once the sensor is mounted and you can walk through the doorway to test it.

  • Single Room Mode: Best for standard rooms where the sensor is only tracking people entering and leaving one space.

  • Dual Room Mode: Used for sensors placed between two tracked rooms (e.g., a hallway and a kitchen). It will update the count for both rooms simultaneously. If you enter the Kitchen from the Hallway, it will increment Kitchen by +1 and decrement the Hallway by -1. This is where the Apex Crosswalk Gateway aggregation comes in. The Crosswalk sensor doesn't keep track of room counts, because rooms can have multiple doorways. All the sensors know is that someone walked under it and the direction they were traveling.

docs.title: 4. Fine Tuning
docs.text:
• Invert Direction: If the sensor counts "Exit" when you are "Entering," use the Invert toggle. You don't need to physically remount the sensor!
  • Next Step: Assembly (Step 3)

docs.title: Step 1: Flashing Your Sensor
docs.text:
The Crosswalk Sensor is the part that goes on your door. You need to flash it before you mount it.

Why we Flash First

To ensure you have the absolute latest features and the most secure, privacy-focused version of our local software, we start every setup by quickly updating the device's firmware. This ensures your sensor is running the most battery-efficient version of our code.

Browser Requirement

You must use Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a computer to flash your device. Other browsers like Safari or Firefox do not support the connection needed.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
• Crosswalk Sensor
  • USB-C Cable
  • Computer with Chrome or Edge installed.
  • Paperclip (a standard one works)

docs.title: Finding the BOOT Button
docs.text: You don't need to open the case to flash the sensor. The BOOT button sits under a small slot on the top of the case, circled below. You'll press it with the end of a paperclip. This is the same on both the Battery-Powered and Hardwired versions.

docs.title: Flashing Procedure
docs.text:
1. Connect: Push a paperclip into the BOOT slot and hold the button down. With the button held down, plug the USB-C cable into the sensor and your computer. Let go of the button once it's plugged in.

  2. Flash: Choose the tab that matches your sensor, then click its Install button.

    Battery-PoweredHardwired

    Install Crosswalk Sensor

    Install Crosswalk Sensor (Hardwired)

    Pick the Right Version

    Both versions use the same chip, so the installer can't tell them apart. Installing the wrong one won't damage anything, but your sensor won't work correctly until you install the version that matches your hardware.

  3. Wait: Do not unplug the sensor until the screen says "Installation Complete".

  4. Ready: Your sensor is now ready to be paired with your Gateway.

  • Next Step: Pairing & Configuration (Step 2)

docs.title: Step 4: Mounting
docs.text: Now that your sensor is configured and verified on the dashboard, it's time to put it on your door.

docs.title: 1. Placement
docs.text:
The Crosswalk sensor uses dual sensing zones to detect direction. Because you can digitally "Invert" the count in the settings, you can mount the sensor in either direction.

  1. Mounting Height: The Crosswalk should be placed at the top of the doorframe, inside the frame, pointing down toward the floor. Place it in the middle of the doorframe, on the inside of the door, so when the door closes it should almost rest up against the sensor.

    Why the top of the frame

    The sensor looks straight down through the doorway, so it sees the top of your head and shoulders as you pass underneath. Mounting it lower, or aiming it across the doorway at body height, will cause missed and miscounted passes.

Far away:

docs.title: 2. Physical Installation
docs.text:
1. Clean the Surface: Wipe the door frame with a dry cloth to ensure a good bond.
  2. Placement: Remove the backing from the adhesive strips and press the sensor firmly against the frame.

  3. Power (Hardwired only): Run a USB-C cable from the sensor to a USB power adapter in a nearby outlet. The sensor needs power at all times, so choose an outlet that isn't switched off with the lights.

    Plan your cable route

    Before you stick the sensor down, make sure your USB-C cable is long enough to reach the outlet. Route it so it stays clear of the door when it opens and closes.

docs.title: 3. Verification
docs.text:
1. Walk Through: Pass through the doorway.
  2. Verify: Check your apex.local dashboard or your smart home app.
  3. Correct Direction: If the count goes the wrong way (e.g., counts -1 when you enter), return to the Configuration Guide and use the Invert toggle to fix it instantly.

Here's the detection in Home Assistant:

  1. Now walk back through in the opposite direction and see the count decrement.

docs.title: Setup Complete!
docs.text:
Your person-counting system is now live.

  • View Support & Help
  • Back to Home Page

docs.title: Crosswalk Sensor Troubleshooting
docs.text: Ensure your occupancy counts are accurate and your sensors are communicating reliably.

docs.title: Understanding the Sensor Lights
docs.text:
The Crosswalk sensor's lights are about power, not status. They never tell you whether the sensor is paired or counting — use your apex.local dashboard or your smart home app for that.

Battery-PoweredHardwired

Once it is running on battery, the sensor keeps every light off so that nothing drains the battery.

LED Color When What it Means 🟡 Yellow Plugged into USB Battery is charging. 🟢 Green Plugged into USB Battery is fully charged. 🔴 Red When you first plug in USB Separate power light — the board has power. It switches off once the sensor enters deep sleep. ⚫ No Lights Running on battery Normal. All lights stay off to save battery.

No lights is normal

On battery power there is no light to tell you the sensor is on or working — this is intentional, and it is how the sensor lasts months on a charge. The only place to check whether a sensor is awake, paired, and counting is your apex.local dashboard or your smart home app.

The Hardwired sensor never sleeps, so its lights stay on whenever it has power.

LED Color When What it Means 🔴 Red Always, while powered The board has power. 🟢 Green Always, while powered Normal. This is the charging light, and it shows green even though there is no battery. ⚫ No Lights Any time The sensor has no power. Check the USB-C cable and power adapter.

docs.title: Installer Can't Find the Sensor
docs.text:
If you click Install and your sensor doesn't appear in the list, or the install fails right away:

  1. Use the BOOT Button: Unplug the sensor. Push a paperclip into the BOOT slot on top of the case and hold it down, then plug the USB-C cable back in. Let go once it's plugged in, then click Install again. See Flashing for a photo of the slot.
  2. Check the Browser: Flashing only works in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a computer.
  3. Check the Cable: Some USB-C cables only carry power, not data. If the sensor still doesn't appear, try a different cable.

docs.title: Count is Backwards or Wrong
docs.text:
If the room count increases when you leave and decreases when you enter:

  1. Digital Invert: Go to your apex.local dashboard, click on the sensor, and toggle the Invert switch. This will instantly fix the direction without you needing to move the hardware. This can be done on the Apex dashboard, or in Home Assistant via MQTT.

  1. Clear Path: Make sure the door doesn't block the sensor when it's open. The sensor needs a clear "line of sight" straight down through the doorway.
  2. Mounting Position: The sensor must sit at the top of the doorframe pointing down at the floor, in the middle of the opening. If it has been mounted lower down or angled across the doorway, it will miss passes. See Mounting for placement.

docs.title: Sensor Won't Pair
docs.text:
1. Gateway Mode: Ensure the Gateway is in Pairing Mode (60-second timer active) before you power the sensor on.
  2. Power Cycle: While the Gateway is searching, unplug the sensor's power and plug it back in — the battery's JST connector on the Battery-Powered version, or the USB-C cable on the Hardwired version. The sensor's lights don't show pairing, so watch the dashboard for confirmation instead.
  3. Proximity: Bring the sensor into the same room as the Gateway just for the initial pairing.

docs.title: Power Loss & Battery Changes
docs.text:
If your sensor's battery dies or you lose power to your house, don't worry!

  • No Re-Pairing Needed: The Gateway remembers your sensors. Once you charge the sensor or the power comes back on, the sensor will automatically find the Gateway again.
  • Auto-Sync: You do not need to click the "Pair" button on the dashboard again for sensors you have already set up.

docs.title: Battery Draining Quickly
docs.text:
This section applies to the Battery-Powered version only.

Charge the sensor by plugging it into USB and waiting for the light to turn from 🟡 Yellow to 🟢 Green.

If a charge isn't lasting as long as you expect:

  1. Check the Link: A sensor that struggles to reach the Gateway has to retry, and retries cost power. Confirm the sensor is reporting reliably on the dashboard.
  2. Move the Gateway Closer: If the doorway is far from the Gateway, or there are several walls between them, relocating the Gateway can make a noticeable difference.
  3. Busy Doorways: A very high-traffic doorway wakes the sensor more often and will shorten the interval between charges.
  • Gateway Troubleshooting
  • View Support & Help
